questions.stem:
The structure of a peptide is given below.
If the absolute values of the net charge of the peptide at pH = 2, pH = 6, and pH = 11 are |z₁|, |z₂|, and |z₃|, respectively, then what is |z₁| + |z₂| + |z₃|?
questions.solution: The peptide is Tyr–Asp–Lys. Its ionisable groups are the N-terminal NH₂, the Lys ε-NH₂, the Asp side-chain COOH, the C-terminal COOH and the Tyr phenol OH. At pH 2 both amines are protonated and both acids are neutral: z = +2. At pH 6 both amines are still NH₃⁺ and both carboxyls are COO⁻: z = 0. At pH 11 both amines are essentially neutral, and both COO⁻ plus the phenoxide (pKa ≈ 10) are negative: z = −3. Sum = 2 + 0 + 3 = 5.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: An organic compound (C₈H₁₀O₂) rotates plane-polarized light. It produces pink color with neutral FeCl₃ solution. What is the total number of all the possible isomers for this compound?
questions.solution: C₈H₁₀O₂ has 4 degrees of unsaturation, which fits a benzene ring. The FeCl₃ colour shows a phenolic OH. The remaining C₂H₅O must contain a stereocentre, and the only option is –CH(OH)CH₃. HO–C₆H₄–CH(OH)CH₃ can be ortho, meta or para, and each is a pair of enantiomers. Total 3 × 2 = 6.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Which of the following plots is(are) correct for the given reaction?
([P]₀ is the initial concentration of P)
P + NaOH → Q + NaBr

options.text: Plot of t₁/₂ (y-axis) versus [P]₀ (x-axis): a horizontal straight line.
Plot of initial rate (y-axis) versus [P]₀ (x-axis): a horizontal straight line.
Plot of [Q]/[P]₀ (y-axis) versus time (x-axis): a curve starting at the origin and bending upwards (slope increasing with time).
Plot of ln([P]/[P]₀) (y-axis) versus time (x-axis): a straight line through the origin with positive slope.

questions.solution: tert-Butyl bromide reacts with OH⁻ by SN1, so rate = k[P] (first order in P only). For a first-order reaction t₁/₂ = 0.693/k, which does not depend on [P]₀ (A correct). The initial rate rises linearly with [P]₀, so B is wrong. [Q]/[P]₀ = 1 − e^(−kt) rises steeply at first and then levels off, not upwards-curving (C wrong). ln([P]/[P]₀) = −kt is a line with negative slope (D wrong).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Consider the following four compounds I, II, III, and IV.
Choose the correct statement(s).

options.text: The order of basicity is II > I > III > IV.
The magnitude of pK_b difference between I and II is more than that between III and IV.
Resonance effect is more in III than in IV.
Steric effect makes compound IV more basic than III.

questions.solution: In IV the bulky NMe₂ lies between two ortho-NO₂ groups, so it twists out of the ring plane (steric inhibition of resonance). Its lone pair is then no longer delocalised into the strongly electron-poor ring. So IV is far more basic than III, while in III the NH₂ lone pair is fully conjugated with three nitro groups (C and D true). The basicity order is II > I > IV > III, so A is false. I and II differ only slightly in pKb, while III and IV differ by many units, so B is false.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Consider the following transformations of a compound P.
P (C₉H₁₂) —(i) NaNH₂ (ii) C₆H₅COCH₃ (iii) H₃O⁺/Δ→ R (Optically active)
P —(i) X (reagent) (ii) KMnO₄/H₂SO₄/Δ→ Q (C₈H₁₂O₆) (Optically active acid)
P —Pt/H₂→ propylcyclohexane (shown)
Choose the correct option(s).
questions.solution: Hydrogenation to propylcyclohexane fixes the carbon skeleton. C₉H₁₂ has 4 degrees of unsaturation: the ring, a ring C=C and a terminal C≡C (needed for NaNH₂ to form an acetylide). Lindlar reduction (X) turns the alkyne into CH=CH₂. KMnO₄ then cleaves both C=C bonds, losing one carbon as CO₂, to give the triacid C₈H₁₂O₆. With the side chain at C4 (A), the triacid has two identical CH₂COOH arms and is achiral. With the side chain at the allylic C3 (C), the product HOOC–CH(CH₂COOH)–(CH₂)₃–COOH is chiral, so P is C. R, made from that P via the acetylide, acetophenone addition and dehydration, must keep the 3-substituted ring, so D (a 4-substituted ring) is wrong.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Consider the reaction sequence from P to Q shown below. The overall yield of the major product Q from P is 75%. What is the amount in grams of Q obtained from 9.3 mL of P? (Use density of P = 1.00 g mL⁻¹; Molar mass of C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0 and N = 14.0 g mol⁻¹)
P —(i) NaNO₂ + HCl / 0-5 °C (ii) 2-naphthol (shown) + NaOH (iii) CH₃CO₂H/H₂O→ Q
questions.solution: P is aniline: 9.3 g ÷ 93 g mol⁻¹ = 0.10 mol. Diazotisation gives benzenediazonium chloride, which couples with alkaline 2-naphthol at C1. Acidification gives the orange-red dye 1-(phenylazo)-2-naphthol, C₁₆H₁₂N₂O (248 g mol⁻¹). At 75% yield: 0.075 × 248 = 18.6 g.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
